en: The Sūtra of the Thousand-Turn Great Illumination Dhāraṇī,
translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, the Court Dispersing Grandee, Acting Assistant Director of the Court of State Ceremonial,
and Dharma-Transmitting Master, the Subject Shi Hu, by Imperial Decree.
Thus have I heard.
At one time the Blessed One was dwelling among the Trāyastriṃśa gods beneath the Pārijātaka tree.
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, [was there].
Together with all the hosts of devas and humans,
they surrounded him from before and behind as they approached the Buddha’s dwelling; each,
with utmost sincerity, joined their palms in homage and took refuge.
They gazed upon the Tathāgata as they stood in succession.
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, came forward and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, I possess a dhāraṇī called the Great Radiance of a Thousand Revolutions."
This dhāraṇī brings great benefit to all worlds. It includes all devas,
nāgas, yakṣas, pretas, kumbhāṇḍas, and so forth, even down to humans and non-humans.
Those who hear this dhāraṇī will all bring all sentient beings under their influence;
all things that are not beneficial shall be entirely eliminated.
"I only pray that the World-Honored One, out of great kindness and great compassion, will grant me permission to proclaim it.
The Buddha said, "O Lord of Devas, excellent, excellent!
It shall be as you have spoken regarding that Mahāsāhasrapramardanī Great Brightness Dhāraṇī."
"You are able to bring great benefit to the world;
you may speak as you wish.
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, [spoke].
Then he spoke the Thousand-Turn Great Illumination Dhāraṇī, saying:
Tadyathā | Nahi tadhye bhāti | Bhagavato | Svādhiṣṭhānādhiṣṭhitāḥ | Sarvabhūtāḥ śṛṇvantu yad ucyate ||1||
They were struck with terror, confusion, and delusion, and fled in retreat.
The yakṣa lord Ratnapāla, Cakrasiddhi, and others manifested various forms and figures,
causing all the bhūtas, yakṣas, and other spirits, as well as those wandering in the air, the vetālas, and the malevolent ghosts of malarial fever to disperse.
Even unto all the poisonous roots of conditioned phenomena and false dharmas—
every harmful act that afflicts sentient beings and fails to bring them benefit—
they are entirely liberated from them.

Maṅgale Sumaṅgale 17. Deliverance from the fear of all kings.
Liberation from the fear of all the transformations and portents of the stars;
liberation from the fear of battle between all one's own and others' military forces;
and liberation from the fear of all weapons.
They are liberated from the fear of all water and fire, such as drowning and burning;
they are liberated from the fear of all evil diseases and afflictions;
they are liberated from the fear of all poisonous harms and injuries.
Fear of lions, fear of elephants,
fear of bears, fear of tigers,
and fear of all predatory beasts and the like.
They are completely liberated from all such fears as the terror of being swept away and drowned in the great ocean, the terror of the profound silence of deep mountains,
and even the terror of the perils of water rapids.
Namo sakṛt saṃkāce saṃkāce kāruṇike kāruṇike naye svāhā. At the time of entering the royal palace, he saw a great minister.
At times while traveling through military camps one encounters enemies;
at times one sees venomous snakes and poisonous dragons;
and at times one meets with yakṣas, piśācas, rākṣasas, and those possessed by uṣmasaras.
Even when amidst mountains, seas, or perilous difficulties, one shall be completely liberated from all such terrors.
Namo Tārāṇīyaṃ hile hile jile jile kapole maṇḍanī svāhā. Furthermore, whether one is seized by royal law, or has one's body firmly bound with shackles, fetters, and manacles;
May all those oppressed by unjust calamities and anxieties be completely liberated.
*Namo dāri dāri uṭāri ṭuri svāhā*. Furthermore, [may they be freed] from whatever is held by the planetary deities (*nakṣatragraha*).
Whether it be through evil dreams, strange portents, or the onset of various illnesses and untimely deaths leading to demise;
or even through strife, disputes, and mutual intimidation—
may they be completely liberated from all such fears.
Namo jvala jvala sarasaraviśara viśara buddhaya buddhaya vidyāya svāhā | rakṣa rakṣa māṃ sarvva...

17. *Dviraṇi svāhā*. Furthermore, all those of evil conduct who perform unwholesome deeds, maintaining heterodox prohibitions and mantras, and performing various incantations and prayers—
May all beings who are deluded, ignorant, crazed, and confused be completely liberated from such conditions as these:

*ru ru ke* (1), *ri lu ke* (2), *tiṣṭha pūrṇaya* (3), *yavāgava* (4), *vimocani* (5), *hrīḥ jriḥ* (6), *kapole* (7), *kaṣṭhāgra sarvataḥ* (8), *sarvabhayebyaḥ svāhā* (9). Blessed One, this is my Great Illumination Mantra of a thousand revolutions.
For example, a wheel-turning sage king possesses a mani jewel called "As One Wishes," by which whatever he desires spontaneously appears before him.
This Great Illumination of a Thousand Revolutions is likewise:
whoever attains it shall be completely liberated from all sufferings and afflictions.
World-Honored One, in the final age, sentient beings will have meager merit.
Not knowing how to take refuge in the Triple Gem,
they recklessly commit transgressions and evils with their body, speech, and mind.
Consequently, the various evil spirits and ghosts of the world find the opportunity to exploit them.
Concealing their own physical forms and manifesting through deceptive transformations,
they afflict and harm sentient beings throughout the day and night,
causing all such beings to undergo various kinds of suffering and distress.
Bhagavān, if there are sentient beings who encounter these evil spirits and suffer from various forms of harassment and affliction,
or even experience any other worldly circumstances that are disagreeable;
One should take seven handfuls of earth from a pure location.
Recite this great vidyā-mantra over each handful seven times to empower it.
Then, knead them together into seven pills and tie them to the corner of one's garment.
It shall cause all malevolent spirits and ghosts who perform unbeneficial acts to dare not approach,
and they shall retreat in fear;
it shall ensure that this person remains peaceful and secure day and night.
All inauspicious things were completely extinguished.
At that time, having spoken this Great Radiant Dhāraṇī of a Thousand Turns,
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, leaped for joy and, together with the hosts of devas, prostrated before the Buddha and withdrew.
The Sūtra of the Thousand-Turn Great Illumination Dhāraṇī
